At each close, compare prior 126-session adjusted-close returns; target SCHD if its return exceeds QQQ, else QQQ; execute at next session open.
column4: Dividend quality firms may hold up better than growth shares when leadership rotates, while QQQ remains the alternative during growth leadership.

column3: At each close, compare prior 126-session adjusted-close returns; target VYM if its return exceeds SPY, else SPY; execute at next session open.
column4: Broad high-dividend stocks may lead in defensive or value-led periods, while SPY captures broad-market leadership.

column3: At each close, compare prior 252-session adjusted-close returns; target DVY if its return exceeds SPY, else SPY; execute at next session open.
column4: A longer relative trend may filter short-lived dividend-factor leadership and capture slower sector allocation changes.

column3: At each close compare SCHD/SPY trailing 126-session returns and DGS10 latest observation dated strictly before the signal session versus its 63-session-prior observation; hold SCHD only when SCHD leads and yield trend is falling, otherwise SPY; execute next open.
column4: Falling long yields can ease valuation pressure on income-oriented equities, potentially extending dividend-quality leadership.

column3: At each close compare VYM/SPY trailing 126-session returns and DGS10 latest observation dated strictly before the signal session versus its 126-session-prior observation; hold VYM only when VYM leads and yield trend is falling, otherwise SPY; execute next open.
column4: A persistent decline in long yields may support dividend assets while relative momentum avoids holding them during broad-market leadership.

column3: At the prior session close, use the known next session calendar date; hold SPY on the last 3 sessions of each month and first 3 of the next month, otherwise SHY; execute next open.
column4: Month-end portfolio rebalancing and payroll or contribution flows may create brief, recurring demand for equities.

column3: At the prior session close, use the known next session calendar date; hold SPY on the last 5 sessions of each month and first 5 of the next month, otherwise SHY; execute next open.
column4: A wider month-boundary window tests whether rebalancing demand persists beyond the final few sessions.

column3: At each prior session close, determine the next session month; hold SPY November-April and SHY May-October, executing at that next open.
column4: Seasonal risk appetite and summer liquidity patterns may leave weaker average equity returns from May through October.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 5% below its value 10 sessions earlier, target SPY for the next 5 sessions then SHY; execute every change at the next open.
column4: Sharp short-window losses can include temporary liquidity shocks that partially reverse over the following sessions.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 7% below its value 10 sessions earlier, target SPY for the next 10 sessions then SHY; execute every change at the next open.
column4: A larger panic threshold may isolate forced selling, with a fixed holding period allowing a rebound to develop.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 8% below its value 20 sessions earlier, target SPY for the next 10 sessions then SHY; execute every change at the next open.
column4: Multiweek drawdowns can overshoot fundamentals as risk limits and stop orders cluster, creating rebound potential.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 10% below its trailing 200-session average, target SPY; otherwise SHY; execute target changes at next open.
column4: Deep discounts to a long-run average may reflect temporary overshooting and mean reversion; this deliberately fades, rather than follows, the existing 200-day trend lane.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 15% below its trailing 200-session average, target SPY; otherwise SHY; execute target changes at next open.
column4: An extreme deviation may better distinguish panic overshoot from ordinary weakness, though signals will be rarer.

column3: At each close, if SPY adjusted close is at least 20% below its trailing 200-session average, target SPY; otherwise SHY; execute target changes at next open.
column4: Very deep dislocations can be followed by unusually strong rebounds as forced liquidation subsides.
